thread:
alex (eng-oncall): heads up — i'm seeing Datadog metrics ingestion latency spike starting ~11:17 UTC. a bunch of host metrics and traces are delayed. alerts are firing but delivery is delayed >5m. paging fired but dashboards look stale. https://status.datadoghq.com/ says partial degradation

datadog-bot: Datadog status: Metrics Ingestion — Degraded performance — https://status.datadoghq.com/incidents/abcd1234 :eyes:

rachel (sre): thanks. are service checks still coming in (heartbeat) or are we missing metrics entirely?

alex (eng-oncall): heartbeats for most services are present but token-bucket/percentiles on http_request_latency are flatlined. traces are arriving in bursts. looks like ingestion queueing on dd side.

mike (product): any customer reports yet? especially from the priority enterprise tenants?

jess (customer-success): got a DM from ACME — they say alert noise and delayed incident notifications back to them. they haven't lost data long-term, but the UI shows "No data" for some panels. escalated to account owner.

rachel (sre): ok plan: 1) enable internal fallback metrics pipeline (cloudwatch/stack) for critical SLO dashboards, 2) increase local retention and verbose logging for exporter agents so we have raw events if dd misses them, 3) open support with Datadog (we need ETA). i'll take 1+2. alex open the support ticket and attach recent aggregator logs.

alex (eng-oncall): on it. creating ticket now. attaching sample curl we used to upload aggregated metrics to our internal store:

```bash
# push last-resort metrics to internal aggregator
curl -X POST "https://metrics-internal.redwood.example/api/v1/ingest" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $INTERNAL_INGEST_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"series": [{"metric":"service.http_request_latency.p50","points":[[1610000000,123]]}]}'
```

ops-bot: PagerDuty: Incident P12345 triggered for team: infra-oncall — severity: P2 — link: https://pagerduty.example/incident/P12345

rachel (sre): alex, when you open DD ticket, request ingestion timeline and cause. ask for buffered data delivery (if available) and whether alerts were backfilled. include sample spans/logs.

alex (eng-oncall): support case created: DD-987654. submitted last 10m of exporter logs and example requests. they replied: "we're seeing elevated queue lengths in US-EAST; investigating". ETA unknown.

mike (product): is this causing customer-visible errors or just monitoring blindspots? need wording for external comms if it becomes a full outage.

jess (customer-success): ACME still in a holding pattern. they'll be nervous if they get duplicate alerts or missed pagings. recommend proactive note if >30m.

rachel (sre): current impact: monitoring/alerts delayed for ~6–12m windows, dashboards may show gaps, but request routing and serving continue. no request failures reported at infra level. classify as observability degraded.

alex (eng-oncall): mitigation steps executed: 1) toggled exporter verbose logging and increased local buffer (see snippet below), 2) switched critical alerts to our internal webhook as fallback, 3) temporarily disabled noisy, non-actionable alerts to reduce alert traffic to Datadog.

```yaml
# exporter config changes
exporter:
  buffer_size: 50000
  flush_interval_seconds: 30
  log_level: debug
```

rachel (sre): i pushed a quick dashboard that reads from CW metrics for the SLOs and pinned it to the incident bridge: https://console.redwood.example/incident/2310009876/dashboard (useful: latency p50/p95, error-rate per-service).

alex (eng-oncall): handing off on-call to rachel for the next 45m — i'm going offline for urgent deploy monitoring. will leave my notes in the incident doc. @rachel — take the bridge and escalate if we see data loss beyond 30m.

rachel (sre): taking it. i'll keep customer comms in the loop. assigning postmortem owner: @alex (will coordinate timeline) and @rachel (will own mitigations section).

datadog-bot: Update on DD-987654: Engineering investigating ingestion queueing. No ETA.

jess (customer-success): sending ACME a short heads-up: "We're seeing degraded monitoring due to a Datadog ingestion issue. Our services are operating normally; we have fallbacks in place and are monitoring closely. We'll update in 30 minutes."

mike (product): good. draft a public status blurb if this continues past 30m, keep it high level (observability degraded, fallbacks active).

rachel (sre): note for follow-ups: 1) evaluate reducing alert noise that amplifies third-party outages, 2) build quicker automated fallback routing to internal metrics store, 3) review runbook to include Datadog support escalation template + canned message for customers.

alex (eng-oncall): leaving handoff notes in the doc. if datadog provides buffered delivery, we'll reconcile and re-ingest. otherwise replay from exporter buffers.

rachel (sre): updating incident status to: observability-degraded -> mitigated (fallbacks active). keeping open until Datadog confirms ingestion recovered and we verify no data loss. will update thread and close when confirmed. :white_check_mark:
